thread:
maria: Hey team, we got a high-severity ticket from a client in APAC. p99 for the new CJK model (redwood-cjk-large-v1) jumped from ~700ms to ~3.1s after the rollout to dedicated pools. Customer: multiple long docs (~20k+ chars) -> big latency. Ticket #INC-20260310-42.

linh: Thanks - any stack traces or headers from their repro?

maria: Pasted what customer sent below. Repro is a single request via the completions API with a long CJK string. They see a sharp spike only for long-context requests. Short prompts fine.

xiaoming (customer): "request id: 9db2f5\nresponse headers:\n  x-rr-latency-ms: 3124\n  x-rr-tokenizer-time-ms: 1278\n  x-rr-kvcache-hit: false\n  x-rr-serving-time-ms: 1790\nlogs:\n  [2026-03-10T04:12:11Z] tokenizer_service.py: tokenize() took 1.28s for 18k chars -> 21600 tokens\n  [2026-03-10T04:12:13Z] runtime: kv cache miss, full decode path used\n  [2026-03-10T04:12:13Z] runtime: decode time 1.7s\n"

ajay: Interesting that tokenizer is taking >1s. Is this new tokenizer variant from onboarding? I recall the onboarding included a new CJK BPE merge table.

linh: Yes, redwood-cjk-large-v1 used the updated BPE merges + a unicode-normalization pass (NFKC) we added to improve repeatability. I wonder if the normalization is expanding some combining marks or causing unusual grapheme splits leading to ~2x token count for certain inputs.

kevin: I pulled the canary traces from staging earlier. On long CJK inputs we see CPU contention on the tokenizer worker threads. Tokenization time correlates strongly with overall p99. Serve GPUs idle longer because CPU blocks on tokenization + KV cache lookup then triggers full decode path.

maria: Customer says it was fine before upgrade (yesterday). They also attached a short program to reproduce. Repro snippet they used: ```curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-cjk-large-v1","prompt":"<long-cjk-payload>","max_tokens":512}'```

linh: Can you paste the exact payload (or a synthetic equivalent)? Need to reproduce locally. If normalization causes string length to increase we should see token_count inflation.

maria: Customer supplied a redacted payload. I'll paste a small synthetic example that still reproduces: a string with mixed CJK + halfwidth/fullwidth punctuation + variation selectors. That combo used to be normalized away but with new NFKC it sometimes expands.

ajay: Quick mitigation we can do immediately: (1) enable model fallback for dedicated pools to redwood-cjk-base-v1 for long-context requests, (2) set a short-circuit to offload tokenization to the fast native tokenizer (if present), (3) add a temporary rate-limit for requests with input_char_count > 12000 until we fix tokenizer perf.

linh: Agreed. Also adding a pre-tokenization NFKC/no-normalize toggle on the request path would let customers choose behavior while we patch the library. I'll prepare a patch to the tokenizer lib to avoid pathological expansion for variation selectors.

kevin: Ops note: rolling back the large-v1 to canary would affect customers using new features. Can we do targeted rollback only for the impacted dedicated pool?

ajay: Yes, we have pool-level model routing. I'll add an emergency routing rule: dedicated-apac -> redwood-cjk-base-v1 for any request with input_char_count > 10k. Apply in 10m.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Created route override rule 8743, will propagate to edge in ~2m.

maria: Customers notified of immediate mitigation and asked to verify. They confirmed initial improvement: p99 dropped to ~850ms after route override.

linh: Next steps: 1) full reproduce locally with the exact payload (I need a sanitized test case) 2) fix tokenizer library to avoid NFKC expansion for CJK variation sequences (owner: linh, ETA 48h) 3) add input normalization toggle/opt-out on API (owner: ajay, ETA 24h for opt-out, 72h for full UI) 4) run canary with patched tokenizer on staging (owner: linh) 5) communicate permanent fix and rollback schedule to affected customers (owner: maria).

maria: Filing a follow-up ticket with owners and timelines. Customer asked for a short-term client-side workaround: pre-normalize to NFC and collapse variation selectors -> suggested snippet: ```python\nimport unicodedata\ndef client_normalize(s):\n    # NFC tends to be closer to what our old tokenizer saw\n    s2 = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)\n    # strip variation selectors (U+FE00..U+FE0F)\n    s2 = ''.join(ch for ch in s2 if not (0xFE00 <= ord(ch) <= 0xFE0F))\n    return s2\n```

kevin: Also adding a telemetry flag to log token_count and tokenizer_time for every request for 48h so we can run histograms. @ops-bot please keep retention for these logs for 7 days.

ops-bot: retention update: tokenization-trace logs retained for 7 days as requested.

maria: Customer validated the workaround and will wait for the permanent patch. Closing initial escalation but keeping thread open until patch is deployed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
